candidate.title: TruSeq PCR Free
candidate.scope: Literal TruSeq PCR Free product-preparation schematic, with no kit version specified: double-stranded DNA passes through fractionation/size selection, end repair/phosphorylation, A-overhang formation, adaptor addition and ligation to a product ready for cluster generation. The single depicted route has no library PCR stage. The biological origin of the input DNA is unspecified; no RNA-to-DNA conversion, clustering or sequencing measurement is depicted. This is schematic architecture rather than a complete experimental protocol.

features: Starting substrate is drawn as two long blue strands with staggered ends.
The biological source of the DNA is not identified in this panel.

evidence.locator: Top: Double-stranded DNA label and long blue duplex

features: A shorter blue duplex represents DNA after the first operation.
The two strands still have offset ends in the drawing.

states.label: End-repaired, phosphorylated DNA fragments
features: Strand ends are drawn aligned after end repair; purple terminal segments first appear at this boundary.
Circled P symbols occur at the upper strand left end and lower strand right end.

evidence.locator: Upper-middle route: End repair / Phosphorylate; downward arrow to aligned blue/purple ends with circled P symbols

states.label: DNA fragments with A overhangs
features: The upper strand right end and lower strand left end carry protruding A symbols.

evidence.locator: Middle route: A-overhang caption and downward arrow to duplex with terminal A and retained circled P symbols

states.label: Y-shaped adaptors supplied for ligation
features: Two opposing adaptor illustrations show the insert-facing orientations at the two insert ends; they are reagent illustrations, not separate assay workflows.

The symbols do not specify full adaptor sequences or the number of independently readable index sequences.

evidence.locator: Plus sign between the A-bearing duplex and the opposed adaptor icons; Add Adaptors caption
evidence.rationale: The plus sign explicitly denotes addition of the drawn adaptors to the insert. A mixture boundary makes that reagent addition distinct from the subsequent ligation; it is not an extra drawn intermediate or a change in insert chemistry.

states.label: Product ready for cluster generation
features: The blue double-stranded DNA insert is flanked by connected colored Y-shaped adaptor structures at both ends.
P5 and P7 labels mark the outer adaptor arms; Index labels remain in the adaptor portions.
The depicted endpoint is a physical DNA library, before the stated cluster-generation interface.
No library PCR operation occurs between adaptor ligation and this endpoint.

operations.label: Fractionate / Size select
operations.description: Convert the long starting double-stranded DNA into shorter fragments and retain a size-selected fragment population. The schematic combines these actions in one caption and does not resolve their internal execution.
operations.information_effect: The library route continues with the retained DNA fragments; the starting long-molecule continuity is not retained in the shorter duplex icon.

evidence.rationale: The shorter DNA icon linked by the first arrow and the size-selection caption support fragmentation and retention of a fragment population, rather than preservation of the starting long-molecule continuity. No quantitative or sequence-specific selection performance is inferred.

operations.label: End repair / Phosphorylate
operations.description: Repair the offset fragment ends to the aligned ends drawn in the next state and add the indicated terminal phosphate groups. The output differs by its repaired terminal segments and circled P symbols.
operations.mechanism: End repair and phosphorylation are named together; no enzyme identities or separate internal reaction order are shown.

evidence.locator: Upper-middle route: End repair / Phosphorylate; downward arrow to aligned blue/purple ends with circled P symbols

operations.label: A-overhang
operations.description: Add terminal A overhangs to the repaired duplex: A symbols appear at the upper-right and lower-left ends while the opposing phosphate symbols remain.
operations.mechanism: Terminal A-overhang formation as labeled; the enzyme is unspecified.

evidence.locator: Middle route: A-overhang caption and downward arrow to duplex with terminal A and retained circled P symbols

operations.label: Add Adaptors
operations.description: Bring the A-overhang DNA and the drawn Y-shaped adaptors together, as indicated by the plus sign. The output records the combined materials before the separately labeled ligation; addition alone does not imply a covalent product.
operations.mechanism: Reagent addition, represented by the plus sign.

operations.label: Adaptor ligation
operations.description: Join the added adaptors to both ends of the DNA insert, producing the connected, adaptor-flanked library shown at the bottom. The central insert remains double stranded and the colored Y arms carry the P5/P7 and Index labels.
operations.mechanism: Adaptor ligation; A on the insert and T on the adaptor depict a compatible terminal interface. Specific ligase chemistry and any unshown finishing steps are not supplied.
operations.information_effect: The physical carrier is the original DNA fragment insert within the adaptor-bearing DNA product. A downstream insert read could establish sequence from retained starting-DNA fragments; the Index labels are adaptor annotations, not evidence of a biological sequence target. The figure supplies a cluster-generation-ready interface but no acquired readout.

Applicability is resolved only for this depicted preparation, not for every product version.
